things_to_do: St. Francis Church and Mattancherry Palace
why_go: January is peak Malabar season — 22–31°C, dry skies ideal for exploring Fort Kochi's colonial lanes and fishing nets. Biennale may open mid-month in even years, anchoring cultural visits.
pack_list: Camera tripod for nets at sunrise

why_go: February is the driest month — 23–32°C with the clearest skies for Chinese Fishing Nets photography. Biennale closing weeks (in cycle years) draw art crowds mid-month. Heritage walks are comfortable dawn-to-dusk.
March retains cool 25–33°C while hotel rates slide 20%. Biennale closing weeks remain active. The last month before pre-monsoon heat collapses outdoor exploration.
why_not: Humidity begins to spike end-month, making afternoon walks uncomfortable.
April heat climbs to 27–34°C with 80% humidity, making outdoor exploration exhausting. Heritage walks collapse mid-day; indoor museums remain accessible but the Malabar experience crumbles.
festivals_this_month: Vishu (April 14) — Kerala New Year closes shops and temples 24h

why_not: Peak pre-monsoon chaos — 28–34°C, 85% humidity, and mid-month thunderstorms. Hotel rates bottom out but the climate defeats outdoor sightseeing. Skip unless visiting for Karkidakam Ayurveda specifically.
Southwest monsoon arrives June 1 with 600–700mm rain and flooding. Heritage sites remain open but waterlogging disrupts exploration and many attractions close seasonally.
Peak monsoon floods Fort Kochi regularly — 700–800mm rainfall makes heritage walks impossible. Many attractions shut. Karkidakam Ayurveda is a specialist visit elsewhere.
Monsoon plus Onam (Aug 25) closes much of the city. 700–800mm rainfall and frequent flooding make outdoor exploration unsafe and unreliable.
festivals_this_month: Onam (August 25, verify 2026) — city shuts, backwaters prioritised over heritage

why_not: Monsoon retreat lingers — 350–400mm rain and oppressive humidity (above 80%) make Fort Kochi's cramped lanes exhaust rather than delight. Heritage walks remain wet.

why_go: October opens the high season — 24–31°C and 200–250mm late spillover. Heritage walks return mid-month with clear skies. Rates hold before November surges.

things_to_do: Chinese Fishing Nets at golden hour
why_go: November builds peak season — 23–30°C, under 50mm rain, and dry skies ideal for sightseeing. Biennale opens mid-December (cycle years), driving November room demand. Book ahead.
December is peak season — 22–30°C, completely dry, and Biennale opens mid-month in even years. Christmas-NYE rates hit 2–3x normal; book 4+ weeks ahead. Expect crowds and premium pricing.
festivals_this_month: Kochi-Muziris Biennale (December mid-month, even years only)

why_go: January is coldest — 5–19°C at 2,133m, perfect for hill-station walks. Kodai Lake, Coaker's Walk, and Pillar Rocks run at full tempo. Post-NYE rates ease January 6 onward.
why_not: Frequent fog obscures hilltop views; early mornings are harsh despite the cold season appeal.

why_go: February holds cool-dry 6–20°C with Bryant Park at year-cleanest bloom. Rates run 25% below January. Trails are clear and flower walks reward dawn departures.
why_not: Frost makes early mornings harsh; afternoon warmth (to 20°C) is more forgiving for mid-day exploration.

why_go: March sustains cool-dry 8–22°C while April crowds haven't yet arrived. Bryant Park builds toward peak bloom. Berijam Lake visibility is year-clearest. Last quiet month before summer migration.
April is year-best — 10–24°C, Bryant Park in full bloom, and summer-migration crowds arriving but rates still reasonable. Trails are dry and flower walks are spectacular.
May is summer-migration peak — 12–24°C, Bryant Park at maximum bloom, and Kurinji flowers (every 12 years, next ~2030) may appear. Rates jump 2–2.5x; expect crowds. Book 4–6 weeks ahead.

why_not: Southwest monsoon onset — 12–21°C with 150–250mm rain and persistent fog. Coaker's Walk obscured, Berijam Lake access erratic. Skip unless rain-walk appeal justifies lower visibility.
Peak Southwest monsoon — 12–20°C, 250–400mm rainfall, and thick fog coating Coaker's Walk and Pillar Rocks. Berijam Lake closes. Trails become muddy and visibility collapses.
Southwest monsoon continues — 12–20°C, 200–300mm rainfall, fog blocks hilltop views. Berijam erratic access, trails muddy. August is the wettest month overall for hill stations.

why_go: September brings monsoon retreat — 11–22°C, 80–150mm rain, and Silver Cascade at year-peak flow from recent rains. Coaker's Walk sightlines return by month end. Solitude returns post-monsoon.
October reopens operations — 10–22°C, 100–180mm residual rain, and Silver Cascade still flowing from monsoon. Sightlines clear rapidly. Trails dry mid-month.
November sustains cold-dry 8–20°C with Coaker's Walk at cleanest views. Bryant Park enters second bloom cycle. Rates climb 25% through month as peak season builds.
December is peak season — 5–19°C, completely dry, and Christmas-NYE rates 2–2.5x normal. Coaker's Walk and Lake draw queues mid-month. Book 4–6 weeks ahead for accommodation.

why_not: Hornbill Festival has just closed; hotels empty, cultural programming stops, and winter quiet (4–18°C) follows the December surge. Unless seeking solitude, visit Oct–Nov instead.
Sekrenyi Festival (Angami tribe) draws crowds and inflates prices despite the dry 5–19°C window. Skip if visiting for solitude or budget concerns.
festivals_this_month: Sekrenyi Festival (February, Angami tribe) — accommodations packed

why_go: March opens spring — 8–22°C, dry weather, and pleasant trekking conditions. Sekrenyi crowds clear. War Cemetery and tribal culture come alive without festival tourism pressure.

why_not: Late April pre-monsoon showers cut treks short and limit hill visibility. While 10–24°C is pleasant, the onset of rains makes trekking unreliable.
Pre-monsoon rains peak while Dzukou lily blooms — trails turn muddy, cancelling trekking plans even as wildflower photography tempts. Skip for reliability.
Monsoon onset brings heavy rain and landslides on hill roads — travel becomes hazardous and treks dangerous. Road impassability blocks access.
Peak monsoon — roads become impassable despite the Dzukou lily bloom. Landslides and flooding make travel unsafe.
Monsoon continues with heavy rains flooding roads and isolating villages. Travel remains hazardous and unreliable.
Lingering monsoon rains cloud visibility and trails remain waterlogged. Trekking reliability low despite improving weather trend.

why_go: October opens post-monsoon season — 10–22°C, clear skies, and green hills. Trekking resumes with dry trails. War Cemetery and cultural exploration shine.
November sustains cool 8–20°C with clear skies. Hornbill buzz builds — accommodation still available before December. Trekking conditions ideal.
December IS Hornbill season — 4–18°C, the 10-day festival at Kisama Heritage Village draws all 16 Naga tribes. Traditional dances, Naga wrestling, fire-eating, and food fairs anchor the visit.
festivals_this_month: Hornbill Festival (December 1–10) — Northeast India's flagship cultural event

things_to_do: State water transport cruise to Alleppey
why_go: January is peak Malabar — 23–31°C, dry, and Ashtamudi Lake (Ramsar Wetland) calm for canoe trips. The 8-hour Kollam-Alleppey state cruise runs daily — India's longest scheduled backwater journey.
February is driest — 24–32°C with Munroe Island canoe trips at year-best. Ashtamudi Lake visibility pristine. Backwater colors sharpen with clear skies.
March is cool-dry 25–33°C with Munroe Island and lake access prime. Hotel rates slide 20%. Alleppey cruise still daily. Last month before April heat crowds.

why_not: April pre-monsoon heat — 27–34°C, 80% humidity, and Munroe Island canoes dawn-only. Backwater journeys become exhausting rather than leisurely. Vishu (Apr 14) shuts shops.
Peak pre-monsoon — 28–34°C, 85% humidity, and arriving thunderstorms blur backwater views. Hotel rates bottom-out but the climate defeats leisure exploration.
Southwest monsoon arrives — 600–700mm rain, beaches unsafe, and cruising in 6–8 hour deluges grim. Backwater tours unreliable mid-month onward.
Peak monsoon — 700–800mm rain, state water transport reduces frequency, and Munroe canoes close. Floods make July travel risky and transport unreliable.
Monsoon rains peak in August — 500–600mm rainfall, Munroe canoes still closed, and outdoor activities unreliable. Onam (Aug 25) shifts focus to celebrations over backwater tourism.
festivals_this_month: Onam (August 25, verify 2026) — shuts shops and shifts focus

why_not: Monsoon showers still disrupt daily plans — 350–400mm rain. Though cruises rebuild operations between downpours, overhead skies and humidity persist.

why_go: October opens the season — 24–30°C, 200–250mm late-monsoon spillover, and Munroe canoes reopen. Backwater operations rebuild mid-month with clearer skies.
November builds peak — 23–30°C, under 50mm rain, and Ashtamudi at year-best. Hotel rates 20% below December. Alleppey cruise daily. Book early.
December is peak season — 22–30°C, completely dry, and Christmas-NYE rates 1.8–2.2x. Ashtamudi Lake and cruises run at full capacity. Book 4+ weeks ahead.
January opens Nilgiri season — 9–22°C at 1,850m with Catherine Falls and Kodanad viewpoint fully accessible. Less crowded than Ooty. Sullivan Memorial and tea-estate walks shine.
why_not: January's late sunrise cuts into morning mist walks when visibility is thickest.

why_go: February is driest — 11–23°C with tea-estate visibility cleanest post-harvest. Toda village walks at year-best clarity. Rates 15% below January. Longwood Shola emerges pristine.
why_not: Tea estates are dormant post-harvest; minimal activity to observe compared to peak plucking season.

why_go: March sustains cool-dry 12–25°C. Longwood Shola visibility cleanest before monsoon. Last quiet month before April spillover from Ooty. Tea estates prepare for new season.
April sustains pleasant 14–27°C with tea estates at year-clearest. Summer-migration spillover from Ooty arrives but Kotagiri remains quieter. First 15 days offer best trekking before haze.
May carries summer-migration spillover — 16–27°C. First fortnight remains clear for trekking and tea drives. Last 10 days bring Southwest-monsoon advance squalls. Quieter than Ooty despite crowds.

why_not: Southwest monsoon onset — 14–22°C, 200–300mm rain, and Kodanad viewpoints fogged. Longwood Shola access restricted. Skip unless rain-walk appeal justifies reduced visibility.
Peak Southwest monsoon — 14–20°C, 500–800mm rainfall, and trails become impassable. Longwood Shola closed. Kodanad views completely obscured by cloud.
Southwest monsoon continues — 14–20°C, 400–600mm rainfall, and trails muddy. Longwood Shola access erratic, viewpoints fogged, and tea-estate visibility poor.

why_go: September brings monsoon retreat — 12–22°C, 100–200mm rainfall, and Catherine Falls at year-peak from recent rains. Tea estates greenest. Clear-sky windows lengthen.
October opens full operations — 11–22°C, 100–150mm residual rain, and Catherine Falls still flowing from monsoon. Tea estates remain lush. Viewpoint sightlines clear rapidly mid-month.
November sustains cold-dry 10–21°C with tea-estate visibility cleanest of the year. Kodanad sightlines at year-best. Rates climb 20% through month as peak season builds.
December is peak season — 8–21°C, completely dry, and Christmas-NYE rates 1.8–2.2x. Still quieter than Ooty/Coonoor. Book 2–3 weeks ahead for accommodation.
January opens peak coastal Kerala — 22–30°C, calm seas, and Lighthouse Beach full with shack capacity. Post-NYE rates ease January 5 onward. Ayurveda and beach yoga anchor the stay.

things_to_do: Hawa Beach and Samudra Beach exploration
why_go: February is driest — 23–31°C with sea at 27°C, ideal for swimming. Lighthouse Beach quieter Tue–Thu. Walk-in rates ease 15%. Three crescent bays at year-cleanest.
March is cool 24–32°C with sea at 28°C, swimmable and warm. Lighthouse, Hawa, and Samudra bays all accessible. Hotel rates ease 25% toward April.

why_not: April pre-monsoon heat — 26–34°C, 75% humidity, and mid-day unbearable. Beach-goers shift to dawn and dusk. Vishu (Apr 14) cultural anchor exists but not enough for the full visit.
festivals_this_month: Vishu (April 14) — temple closures affect heritage visits

why_not: Peak pre-monsoon — 27–35°C, 80% humidity, and pre-monsoon swells keep swimmers out mid-month. Sea at 30°C is bathable but thermally exhausting on the sand.
Southwest monsoon arrives — 700–900mm rain, beaches unsafe, shacks shut, and lighthouse climb suspended. Accommodation rates spike without better weather offset.
Peak monsoon — 900–1,100mm rainfall, beaches forbidden, and rough seas unsafe for swimming. Karkidakam Ayurveda is a specialist visit elsewhere.
Monsoon continues — 600–800mm rain, beaches unsafe, and rough seas dangerous. August is one of the wettest months on the coast.
festivals_this_month: Onam (August 25, verify 2026) — celebrations shift focus from beach tourism

why_not: Monsoon retreat persists — 250–400mm rain, rough seas, and swimming unsafe. Beach calms gradually by month's end. Shacks rebuild mid-month.

why_go: October opens season — 24–31°C, post-monsoon conditions, and 100–200mm late rain. Seas remain choppy until late-month. Shacks rebuilt by mid-October. Rates hold before November surge.
why_not: Seas remain choppy until late October, limiting safe swimming and water activities.

why_go: November builds peak — 22–30°C, completely dry, and Lighthouse Beach at full shack capacity. Sea at 27°C, perfect for swimming. Hotel rates 20% below December.
December is peak season — 21–30°C, sea at 27°C, and Christmas-NYE Dec 22–Jan 5 rates double. Lighthouse promontory gridlocked. Book 4+ weeks ahead.
January opens peak Malabar — 22–31°C, completely dry, and Calicut Beach pier at clean sky. Mishkal Mosque, Kuttichira market, and biriyani-halwa circuit at full hours.
February is driest — 23–32°C with Mishkal Mosque, Kuttichira market, and Beach heritage at year-clean visibility. Hyatt and Beach Heritage hotels at peak operations.
March retains comfortable 24–33°C. Mosque-market-beach circuit works 7–11am and 5–7pm. Hotel rates ease 20% toward April. Last month before pre-monsoon crowds.

why_not: April pre-monsoon heat — 26–35°C, 75% humidity, and midday exploration taxing. Indoor heritage (Mishkal Mosque) survives but outdoor beach and market circuits collapse. Vishu (Apr 14) shuts most shops 24h.
Peak pre-monsoon — 27–36°C, 80% humidity, and pre-monsoon thunderstorms. Heritage indoors only. Pre-monsoon haze dulls backwater views and outdoor sightseeing.
Southwest monsoon arrival — 700–900mm rain, beaches forbidden, and Kuttichira market suspended. Outdoor heritage circuit impossible.
Peak monsoon — 900–1,100mm rainfall, outdoor circuit dead, and downpours make sightseeing nearly impossible. Indoor heritage halls remain but are not the Kozhikode experience.
Monsoon continues — 600–800mm rain, beaches closed, and Kuttichira market still suspended. Onam (Aug–Sep) brings programming but not enough offset for monsoon weather.
festivals_this_month: Onam (August 25, verify 2026) — celebrates via food and home but not heritage tourism

why_not: Monsoon retreat lingers — 250–400mm rain, heavy monsoon rains limit beach and heritage walks. Kuttichira market resumes by week three but overhead skies persist.

why_go: October opens season — 24–31°C, post-monsoon, and 100–200mm late rain. Full Malabar circuit returns by week two. Kuttichira market and Mishkal Mosque reopen operations.
November builds peak — 22–30°C, completely dry, and Kuttichira market and Mishkal Mosque at year-clean. Paragon at full lunch queue. Book hotels early.
December is peak season — 21–30°C, completely dry, and Christmas-NYE Dec 22–Jan 5 rates climb 50–70%. Paragon needs reservation. Book 4+ weeks ahead.
January opens peak window — 16–28°C, completely dry, and Sarpa Dosha rituals at full schedule. Kumara Parvatha trek is dry, safe, and 13km one-way doable in one long day.
February is driest — 18–29°C with Kumara Parvatha trek at year-best conditions. Sarpa Dosha rituals full schedule. Forest visibility clearest.
March sustains cool 20–31°C with Kumara Parvatha trek workable dawn-only. Humidity 70% allows mid-hike water access. Rates 25% off February.
why_not: March heat peaks at 33°C and dries trek water sources mid-hike.
pack_list: Light shirt and shorts for days

why_not: April pre-monsoon heat — 24–33°C, 78% humidity, and Kumara Parvatha trek becomes brutal. Temple darshan dawn-and-dusk only, midday temple stops.
Peak summer heat — 25–33°C, 82% humidity, and Kumara Parvatha closes mid-month due to heat and water scarcity. Peak summer hits 40°C+, making outdoor temple visits physically taxing.
Southwest monsoon onset — 1,000–1,200mm rain, Kumara Parvatha trek closed, and landslide risk high. Monsoon makes the trek impassable.
Peak monsoon — 1,200–1,500mm rainfall, Kumara Parvatha closed, and roads on landslide watch. Forest trails treacherous. Peak monsoon swells rivers.
Monsoon continues — 900–1,100mm rainfall, Kumara Parvatha closed, and temple access becomes unreliable. Monsoon floods make August travel difficult.
Monsoon retreat — 400–600mm rain persists, trails remain waterlogged and slippery through early September, and Kumara Parvatha stays closed. Trek reopens October mid-month.

why_go: October opens season — 19–29°C, 200–300mm spillover, and Kumara Parvatha reopens mid-month. Pilgrim flow rebuilds. Kumara Parvatha becomes popular again.
November builds peak — 17–28°C, under 70mm rain, and Champa Shashti festival cluster (6-day celebration). Rates climb 20% through month. Trek conditions ideal.

why_go: December is peak season — 16–27°C, completely dry, and Champa Shashti tail celebrations. Kumara Parvatha at year-cleanest conditions. Lock beds 4–6 weeks ahead.
